sections.html: Western-central Africa: Cameroon and Equatorial Guinea, also tributaries of the Ngoko, Congo River system, in Cameroon. Type locality: hills in the Bulu country, some 120 km in the interior from Batanga, at an elevation of between 450–600 m, Cameroon.

The genus Amphilius are all more or less the same when keeping them in aquaria. Water would need to be kept on the cool side for this genus as they inhabit flowing waters in their natural habitat. Species of this genus are not imported very often but would make good aquarium additions if kept in optimum conditions.
Provide a small-grained gravel or sand substrate, and plant the tank well, with a slight current to mimic their natural habitat. Provide rockwork and caves.
Mosquito larvae, Tubifex, Cyclops, Daphnia, grindal worms, vegetable food, tablet and flake.

Etymology: the specific name longirostris comes from longus, long, and rostris, snout, which projects a little beyond the lower jaw.

Diagnosis: caudal fin with 7+8 principal rays; caudal peduncle 1.6–2 times longer than deep; snout longer than post-orbit length; eyes placed distinctly nearer to the hind margin of the head than to the tip of the snout.

IUCN: widespread or without major threats throughout the Central Africa assessment region and assessed as Least Concern (IUCN 2010, needs updating).
